newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Zedillo, Ortiz outline new economic plan.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Zedillo, Ortiz outline new economic plan.

text.p: Mexico's President Ernesto Zedillo and Finance Minister Guillermo Ortiz on Tuesday outlined the government's new economic program that will run until the year 2000.
Zedillo made his address at Los Pinos, the president's residence, while Ortiz spoke to reporters there just before the speech.
-- Ortiz said the government expects gross domsetic product to grow by 4.8 percent in 1998, 5.2 percent in 1999 and reach 5.6 percent in 2000.
-- Zedillo said the government is aiming for average GDP growth of five percent a year.
-- Ortiz said Mexico is targeting an increase in private savings to 18 percent of gross domestic product by 2000.
-- Ortiz said the government wants to use external savings only as a complement to internal savings.
-- Ortiz said there would not be any other financial crisis in this administration.
-- He said no artificial anchors would be used to control inflation.
-- Zedillo said the new program would seek to create one million jobs annually until 2000.
-- Zedillo said that inflation in May could be less than the 1.08 percent seen in April.
-- Zedillo said that Mexico has created 1.15 million jobs in the last 21 months.
-- Ortiz said investment should reach 25 percent of GDP by the year 2000, consistent with GDP growth above 5.0 percent.

-- He added that the 25 percent would consist of a 22 percent level of internal savings and three percent from external savings. In the internal sector, 18 percent would come from private savings and four percent from public savings.
The plan the president and finance minister outlined is officially known as the National Program for Financing Development (Pronafide).
